title: A derived morphism descends to a common finite coefficient field
statement: Fix a prime l, a field Ω algebraically closed over the l-adic field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and two finite intermediate coefficient fields E and F [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Let A in D(E) and B in D(F) have bounded finite-dimensional cohomology [def-weil-point-fd-complexes]. Write T for actual derived scalar extension [def-weil-finite-dimensional-complex-scalar-extension], and c for its canonical tower comparison [lem-weil-derived-field-scalar-extension-tower]. For every f : T_{Ω/E} A → T_{Ω/F} B, there exist a finite coefficient field N containing E and F and g : T_{N/E} A → T_{N/F} B such that f = c_{Ω/N/E,A}^{-1} ≫ T_{Ω/N}(g) ≫ c_{Ω/N/F,B}.

source.place: Order 1509, display defining D^b_fd(Qbar) as the finite coefficient 2-colimit; the Hom-surjectivity argument of def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category.

proof.text: Use the cohomology-model and Hom-bijection clauses of [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] over E, F and the closure. The finite-support predicate [def-weil-point-fd-complexes] means only finitely many cohomology spaces contribute. Choose finite bases for these spaces. By [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension] their scalar-extended bases identify the given morphism with finitely many matrices over the closure.

For each of the finitely many matrix entries use exhaustion by finite subextensions in [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Take the iterated compositum of these fields and E and F, using directedness in the same statement. This gives one finite coefficient field N containing E, F and every matrix entry. An empty family of entries needs only the compositum of E and F.

Regard each matrix as a map between the N-extensions of the chosen E- and F-cohomology spaces. Through the cohomology comparisons of [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension], this is a family of maps between the cohomology spaces of the N-extended derived objects. Outside the finite support take zero. Surjectivity of the Hom-bijection of [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] over N supplies the derived morphism g.

Apply cohomology to the stated conjugation of the scalar extension of g. The tensor tower comparison of [lem-weil-derived-field-scalar-extension-tower] and its cohomology compatibility in [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension] identify each of its matrices with the original matrix of f: on basis vectors the coefficients are just included from N into the closure. Injectivity of the Hom-bijection over the closure in [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] proves the required equality.

lean.statement:
theorem pointFd_morphism_descent
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω]
    [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω]
    (E F : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω)
    (A : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} E.val))
    (B : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} F.val))
    (hA : pointFiniteDimensional E.val A) (hB : pointFiniteDimensional F.val B)
    (f : (fieldDerivedScalarExtension (K := E.val) (L := Ω) E.val.subtype).obj A ⟶
      (fieldDerivedScalarExtension (K := F.val) (L := Ω) F.val.subtype).obj B) :
    ∃ (N : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω) (hE : E ≤ N) (hF : F ≤ N)
      (g : (fieldDerivedScalarExtension
          (IntermediateField.inclusion (E := E.val) (F := N.val) hE).toRingHom).obj A ⟶
        (fieldDerivedScalarExtension
          (IntermediateField.inclusion (E := F.val) (F := N.val) hF).toRingHom).obj B),
      f = (fieldScalarTower
          (IntermediateField.inclusion (E := E.val) (F := N.val) hE).toRingHom
          N.val.subtype).inv.app A ≫
        (fieldDerivedScalarExtension (K := N.val) (L := Ω) N.val.subtype).map g ≫
        (fieldScalarTower
          (IntermediateField.inclusion (E := F.val) (F := N.val) hF).toRingHom
          N.val.subtype).hom.app B
